title: Cost Baseline Archaeology: establish workload econ baselines and lineage for batching/caching/quantization
creator: Aarav Kapoor
description: Why: We lack consistent, workload-specific cost baselines that tie concrete serving knobs (batch size, prefix/KV cache TTL, quant profile) to downstream unit economics and user-observed latency. This makes rollouts risky and A/B experiments noisy. Goal: build a repeatable baseline archaeology process that reconstructs per-route and per-customer econ baselines, clearly attributes cost changes to specific knobs, and produces lineage artifacts usable by Console, Autoscaler, and Release controls. Scope: - ingest historical traces (token length distributions, latency P99, model variant, batch distributions) - generate per-route baseline reports (cost/token, cost/request, latency SLO risk) - surface change lineage for each optimization applied (who flipped what, when, observed delta) - integrate baseline artifacts into rollout gating and the Optimize recommendations engine
acceptance_criteria: 1) Baseline generator produces stable per-route baseline reports for top-200 routes by volume; 2) Each baseline includes token-econ, latency SLO risk score, and recommended safe knob ranges; 3) Changes to knobs are recorded with lineage metadata and viewable in Console; 4) Two pilot rollouts (one batching, one quantization) use baselines to automatically select safe config and show >=8% net token-cost reduction without exceeding latency SLOs for the pilot cohort.
metrics: baseline_coverage_percent: percent of top routes with baselines
pilot_cost_reduction_percent: delta token cost for pilot cohorts
slo_breach_delta: P99 latency delta compared to baseline
lineage_trace_rate: percent of changes with lineage metadata
